chunks: And from him, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who manumitted his slave by deed (dabbara) and then needed the money for its price. He said, and he said: 'He is his slave; if he wishes, he can sell him; and if he wishes, he can free him; and if he wishes, he can keep him until he dies. So when the master dies, the slave is freed from one-third of his estate.'

key_terms.دَبَّرَ: To manumit a slave by deed, making them partially free but still bound to the master until full manumission or death.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a manumitted-by-deed slave if the master dies before fully freeing him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the legal status of a 'dabir' (slave manumitted by deed), affirming the master's discretion to sell, keep, or fully free the slave before death. It establishes that if the master retains the slave until death, the slave attains full freedom, with the manumission cost treated as a debt payable from one-third of the estate, reflecting the Shia jurisprudence on inheritance and manumission obligations.
